subject: Short payment on Invoice INV-2025-09-174 — TDS applied by payer; request for reissued invoice/credit
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@oakridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Oakridge Analytics AR <payables@oakridge.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:12:00 +05:30
Subject: Short payment on INV-2025-09-174 — TDS applied by payer

Hi Marcus,

We processed payment for INV-2025-09-174 yesterday but the payment was remitted net of 10% TDS per our local tax rules. Our bank remittance reference is ORG-20251103-01 (attached).

To reconcile our books we need one of the following from Redwood:
- A reissued invoice that clearly shows the gross amount and the TDS withholding line so our AP can match payment and file the deduction; OR
- A signed credit note showing the withheld amount and a short explanation so our accounting can clear the liability.

We have attached the remittance and a scanned copy of the TDS deposit slip issued by the tax office. If you can confirm which route you prefer, we will release the remaining amount or provide additional documentation as required.

Apologies for the short payment — this was applied by our local AP team to comply with regulation, not a dispute of services.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Finance Manager
Oakridge Analytics
Attachments: remittance_20251103.pdf, tds_deposit_slip_oakridge_2025.jpg
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@oakridge.com>
Cc: Oakridge Analytics AR <payables@oakridge.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short payment on INV-2025-09-174 — TDS applied by payer

Aisha —

Thanks for the note and for sending the remittance. I appreciate the context. I’ve looped in our finance and tax leads so we can confirm the cleanest path forward. Quick questions while we triage:

- Can you confirm the exact gross invoice amount and the net amount received (bank reference helps but a short remittance detail is helpful)?
- Is Oakridge requesting a formal credit note that we post to your account, or would you prefer a reissued invoice that explicitly shows the withholding line?

We typically offer two options depending on customer preference and local tax implications:
1) We issue a credit memo for the withheld amount and leave the original invoice intact (fast; no cash movement from us).
2) We reissue a corrected invoice showing the gross and the withholding, then settle the ledger once we receive the TDS tax receipt (can support your reclaim).

Cc’ing Priya (AR) and Mina (Tax) to propose the exact wording/attachments required and turnaround.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0193
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@oakridge.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short payment on INV-2025-09-174 — TDS applied by payer

Hi Aisha / Marcus,

Thanks for the attachments — we received the remittance PDF and the TDS deposit slip. Quick internal note for transparency: Oakridge withheld 10% (INR equivalent) at payment time which created a short payment on our ledger. To resolve cleanly, finance and tax recommend either:

Option A (preferred for speed):
- Redwood issues a credit memo equal to the short-paid amount (CR-INV-174-2025). That clears the AR balance on our side immediately.
- Oakridge keeps the TDS receipt for local filing; no cash refund from Redwood.
- We attach a short explanation on the credit memo: "Amount short-paid due to statutory withholding by payer. Customer provided TDS deposit proof."

Option B (preferred by customers that need a reissued gross/net invoice):
- Redwood reissues a corrected invoice that shows gross and a separate withholding line for the 10% TDS.
- Oakridge can continue to report gross and attach the TDS deposit slip. If Oakridge needs a refund for the withheld amount to be paid by Redwood (rather than crediting), we require official government proof of TDS deposit plus a signed indemnity form. Refunds may take up to 10 business days after verification.

Attached I’m including a draft credit memo (proposed_credit_memo_INV-2025-09-174.pdf) for your review. If you confirm Option A we’ll post the credit memo today and reflect it against INV-2025-09-174. If you prefer Option B we’ll prepare the corrected invoice and outline the documentation needed for any outbound refund.

Mina: any additional tax wording we should include in the memo/invoice?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior AR Analyst, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_credit_memo_INV-2025-09-174.pdf
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@oakridge.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short payment on INV-2025-09-174 — TDS applied by payer

Hello Priya / Marcus,

Thanks for the clear options — Oakridge prefers Option B (reissued invoice) so our tax team has the gross/net document for local filings. We are not requesting a refund; we just need the corrected invoice that explicitly shows: gross amount, TDS withheld (10%), net paid, and a short freeform line: "Payment received net of statutory TDS withheld by payer (reference ORG-20251103-01)."

Attached is the TDS deposit confirmation (tds_certificate_oakridge_2025.jpg). Please reissue the corrected invoice and confirm the invoice number/version you will use. Once we receive the corrected invoice, our AP will mark the invoice as matched and close the short payment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best regards,
Aisha Khan
Finance Manager
Oakridge Analytics
Attachments: tds_certificate_oakridge_2025.jpg
